ReflexFoundry
related.content: **Teach agents which decisions no longer need expensive deliberation.** ReflexFoundry finds repeated, bounded decisions in explicitly shared workflow records, adapts a local [Laya](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya) decision head, and checks whether using it would improve independently verified task outcomes. It includes a small Python CLI, an offline evidence laboratory, and a Codex skill integration. A fast model can still make a workflow slower or less reliable. ReflexFoundry includes startup and fallback costs, compares against a transparent heuristic, and blocks deployment when the evidence fails. A rejected policy is a useful result. **v0.1.1 experimental preview.** The executed benchmark concerns validation of supplied coding patches in generated Python repositories. It does not establish improvements in autonomous coding, production repositories, subscription usage, dollars, or energy. Context retrieval has a typed specification, but the first evaluator and trained-policy workflow cover test scope. See the [research basis](docs/research.md) and [evaluation boundaries](docs/evaluation.md). The [0.1.1 fixes](CHANGELOG.md) tighten validation and shadow evidence; the original model and benchmark remain withheld and unchanged. ## Try it without a model Python 3.11 or newer. No API key, paid service, or model download is needed for this path. ```bash git clone https://github.com/nazeeh111/ReflexFoundry.git cd ReflexFoundry python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e . reflex specs reflex benchmark --output runs/first-look --small reflex discover --workspace runs/first-look reflex lab --workspace runs/first-look --output runs/first-look/lab.html ``` Open the generated `lab.html`, or run `reflex serve --workspace runs/first-look` for the local, read-only Lab. The small demo executes real checks on fresh generated fixtures. It is intentionally too small for model promotion. Each benchmark run needs a fresh output directory. For a complete walkthrough, use the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md). To inspect the already trained research head without retraining, follow the [model artifact guide](docs/model-artifacts.md). Package installation is from source; a PyPI publication is not implied. ## What the tool does | Stage | Evidence produced | | --- | --- | | **Observe** | Explicitly authorized records, allowed input fields, redacted common secrets and personal identifiers. | | **Discover** | Recurring supported decision families, choice counts, and an outcome-based opportunity estimate. | | **Train** | A specialized Laya head trained on the training split, with hashes and provenance. | | **Evaluate** | Separate calibration, promotion and test groups; task outcomes, timing, uncertainty, and baseline comparisons. | | **Shadow** | Local proposals with the original fallback still returned. Candidate outcomes require independent checking. | | **Deploy** | Explicit, bounded opt-in only after the held-out gate and verified shadow evidence pass. | | **Monitor** | Recorded outcomes, artifact identity, input drift checks, abstention, decision budgets, and rollback history. | Discovery starts with two predefined decision families. It does not infer arbitrary new APIs or discover hidden internal reasoning.

related.name: KERNELDARWIN
related.content:
# KERNELDARWIN ### Why is this GPU program slow? Keep the experiment that answers it. An evidence-first performance investigation laboratory. Profile a bounded workload, keep competing explanations, test targeted Triton configurations, and preserve the numerical checks and timing uncertainty behind each decision. **v0.2.0 is a research preview.** The development host is an Apple M4, with no NVIDIA CUDA device. The release includes actual CPU control experiments, a fitted CPU intervention selector, and a prepared CUDA/Triton execution path. **No GPU speedup, GPU-trained policy, causal GPU diagnosis, sanitizer pass, or GPU superiority is claimed.** [Validation status →](docs/validation.md) [Explore the LAB](https://nazeeh111.github.io/KERNELDARWIN/) · [Quickstart](#try-the-laboratory) · [Research](docs/research.md) · [Methodology](docs/methodology.md) · [Releases](https://github.com/nazeeh111/KERNELDARWIN/releases) ![Actual LAB overview with an explicitly labeled CPU control, paired latency distribution and verification ledger](docs/assets/v0.2/lab-desktop.png) ## One investigation, all the evidence The shipped controls compare a higher-precision NumPy reference with batched float32-intermediate implementations within declared tolerances. They exercise the same record, correctness, paired timing, confirmation and learning components used by the CUDA path. They are **CPU software controls**, not evidence of GPU optimization. The reproducible suite contains **24 workloads, 72 attempted interventions, four operation families and six shapes**, including strided inputs and no-improvement cases. Raw measurements, failed decisions, source identities and a trained model live in [the evidence directory](evidence/cpu-2026-10-26/). [Read the measured result and its limits](docs/results.md). The LAB now places the measured latency fingerprint and verification ledger together, with a keyboard-accessible timing-pair inspector, parent-aware candidate history, and synchronized evidence selection. Its self-hosted IBM Plex typography and interruptible, reduced-motion-aware transitions serve the investigation. The LAB lets you follow the useful questions: what was measured, which explanation remains plausible, what changed, and what passed independent confirmation? GPU timelines, utilization and rooflines stay unavailable when their required measurements are absent.

[Watch the current workbench recording](docs/assets/v0.2/workbench.mp4). The [original v0.1 demo](docs/demo/brag.mp4) is preserved. The current v0.2 workbench has a redesigned interface with paired-sample inspection, linked candidate selection, accessible lineage, and source comparison. CPU control playback remains labeled; it is not live GPU optimization. ## Try the laboratory Python 3.11 or later. Basic installation has no runtime dependencies or model-provider credentials. ```bash git clone https://github.com/nazeeh111/KERNELDARWIN.git cd KERNELDARWIN python -m pip install . kd doctor kd lab # Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 ``` The public LAB is static and reads recorded JSON. It never compiles or executes uploaded code. Import a record or inspect the bundled controls. No public GPU execution service is exposed. For actual local CPU controls: ```bash python -m pip install '.[control]' kd control --family softmax --shape 128 1024 --store .runs kd train --store evidence/cpu-2026-10-26/records --device-kind cpu --output .runs/cpu-model.json python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

related.name: ReplaySmith
related.content:
**Turn a demonstrated browser task into a reusable workflow with inputs, recovery evidence, and an outcome you can verify.** Run it locally, inspect why an element was chosen, and export the same behavior as Playwright code or an Agent Skill. No model, API key, account, or subscription required.

Download · Workflow guide · Benchmarks · Prior art · Contribute

![Actual ReplaySmith studio demonstration](assets/demo.gif) ## Try it in two minutes Requires **Node.js 22+** on macOS, Linux, or Windows. The release contains the built CLI and studio; you do not need a compiler. ```sh npm install --global https://github.com/nazeeh111/ReplaySmith/releases/download/v0.1.0/replaysmith-0.1.0.tgz replaysmith install-browser replaysmith studio ``` Open the printed loopback URL, usually `http://127.0.0.1:3333`. The example is a real local form with a saved-note assertion. Change the **note** input and choose **Run workflow**. The report distinguishes actions completing from an outcome being verified. On Linux, install Chromium's OS libraries with `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` if the browser installer reports missing dependencies. Release packages are hosted on GitHub; this project is not published to the npm registry. Prefer source? ```sh git clone https://github.com/nazeeh111/ReplaySmith.git cd ReplaySmith npm ci npx playwright install chromium npm run studio ``` ## Demonstration → dependable replay 1. **Record or import.** Demonstrate in a fresh Chromium window, or import Chrome DevTools Recorder JSON. Captured form values become named input defaults automatically. Unsupported import operations fail visibly. 2. **Understand and improve.** Inspect every step, locator, fingerprint, origin, and input. Edit the workflow in the studio or as versioned JSON. Mark consequential actions as sensitive. 3. **Verify and replay.** Add a final text, value, URL, or visibility check that expresses the intended result. Run with new inputs; inspect failures, abstentions, and candidate evidence. 4. **Export.** Download executable Playwright JavaScript or a directory-compatible Agent Skill. The export embeds the same guards, scorer, and outcome checks. Use **Assert text** while recording to capture a result, then **Stop & review**. Recording is one tab, one origin, with a clean browser profile. It does not attach to your normal signed-in browser. ![ReplaySmith workflow studio](assets/studio.png)
